correctness.rationale: For stationary Poisson/exponential FCFS arrivals with two consecutive tags conditioned originally susceptible, PASTA gives geometric Q and Q1. The first marginal is obtained by integrating out the next exponential arrival and future marked Poisson thinning; the second marginal uses the first known-susceptible predecessor. For the joint law, the no-intervening-arrivals property reduces escape to E[(1-p)^Q a^(Q1+1)]. The geometric potential-service-event kernel Q1=(Q+1-G)_+ yields an absolutely convergent double series and the exact rational expression; direct algebra gives the positive covariance and simple Pearson correlation. All denominators positive for 0<p,ρ<1, all event conditioning explicit. An independent exact-rational grid with bounded finite-tail tests and forward path simulations corroborates, not substitutes for, the complete proof.

value.rationale: The zero-duration-contact boundary is a canonical limiting observable of the new contagious-queue model. Tracking two *successive* susceptible customers tests a qualitatively new question: dependence of actual infection outcomes, not the chance for one tagged customer. The rational correlation reveals provable positive clustering for all admissible parameters and nonzero heavy-traffic correlation despite vanishing escape probability; the exact pair infection-count variance inflation factor quantifies why an independence assumption miscalibrates uncertainty. It is an intrinsically motivated complete bivariate law, not an arbitrary fixed-size enumeration or renamed single-customer formula. Positive exposure thresholds and broader service laws remain outside the result.
